landingHeroSub: SMSWithoutBorders (SWOB) is dedicated to researching, developing and promoting secure and accessible communication tools that function even without an internet connection.

About.description: SMSWithoutBorders (SWOB) is dedicated to researching, developing and promoting secure and accessible communication tools that function even without an internet connection.
About.description1: The development includes mobile apps for various platforms such as Android, iOS and Linux systems. Some of the work also includes white papers on topics such as cryptography, communications and internet freedom.
About.description2: The journey toward achieving our mission began in 2021 with the development of the first Android version of RelaySMS. We have come far since then, with support for more platforms and many more apps.
About.description3: We publish our research as frequently as possible on our blog and make announcements via our social media outlets. SMSWithoutBorders is a project started by the team at Afkanerd.

projectHeadline: Everything we build, open and free
projectSubHeader: SMSWithoutBorders builds open-source internet freedom tools that protect free speech and help people bypass internet censorship and shutdowns.
papersBody: The team publishes research papers and notes behind the stack, from architecture and encryption to threat modeling.
projectsResilienceTitle: Built on SMS - the most resilient layer
projectsResilienceBody: SMS works when data doesn't. We built an entire secure relay infrastructure on top of it, so people can stay connected regardless of what the network - or a government - does.
developerLibrariesBody: All core components are open-source and reusable.

projectDescriptions.relaysms: A mobile application that bridges SMS networks with internet-based messaging services. Connected platform credentials are stored securely on your device, allowing messages to be delivered through SMS when internet access is unavailable.
projectDescriptions.dekusms: An open-source, end-to-end encrypted SMS app for Android. Powers RelaySMS's SMS-handling layer, and can also be used standalone as a secure replacement for your default SMS app. Supports MMS image sending.
projectDescriptions.vault: Secure access token management system for message publishing. Protects OAuth2 credentials with an additional encryption layer.
projectDescriptions.gateway: Enables users to synchronize and communicate with the publisher module. The backbone relay infrastructure between devices and the backend.
projectDescriptions.bridge: Allows users to communicate with online platforms via SMS entirely, without needing any internet. Enables a secure handshake and encrypted exchange over SMS only.
projectDescriptions.publisher: Middleware sitting between Gateway and backend. Pluggable PNBA adapters for Telegram and other platforms. Handles decryption and routing.

libraryDescriptions.smsmms-library: Android SMS and MMS transport library used by RelaySMS and DekuSMS. Handles carrier messaging flows, runtime permissions, MMS sending, and default-SMS integration.
libraryDescriptions.lib-image: Image helper library for MMS and media processing in the mobile messaging stack. Used by both RelaySMS Android and iOS.
libraryDescriptions.rusty_relaysms_payload_specs: Implementation of the RelaySMS specifications paper and security implementation details from the technical paper.
libraryDescriptions.double-ratchet-java: Android encryption helper library implementing Signal Double Ratchet primitives for mobile apps in the RelaySMS stack.
libraryDescriptions.double-ratchet-python: Python cryptography library implementing Signal Double Ratchet and supporting helpers for secure exchange across backend services.
libraryDescriptions.double-ratchet-ios: Swift implementation of SMSWithoutBorders' Signal Double Ratchet cryptography helpers for secure message exchange on iOS.
libraryDescriptions.image-android: Android image helper library used for MMS and media processing in the mobile messaging stack.
libraryDescriptions.image-ios: Swift image-processing helper library for RelaySMS iOS media workflows and attachment handling.
libraryDescriptions.gateway-client: Remote Python client for interacting with the Gateway layer from external tools and services.
libraryDescriptions.adapter-interface: Pluggable interface for adding new platform bridges. Telegram is the reference PNBA adapter and the same publisher layer supports additional platform adapters.

project1.title: RelaySMS
project1.description: RelaySMS uses SMS messaging to communicate with online platforms without needing an internet connection. The users can grant access to their online platforms which would be used to act on their behalf using SMS messaging. The access granted, messages being sent from the app, and how they get published online are secured with strong up-to-date cryptographic and security practices.

project2.title: DekuSMS
project2.description: DekuSMS is an Android SMS messaging app. It enables 2 users of the app to communicate using end-to-end encryption over SMS messages. The app also contains message forwarding abilities supporting protocols such as SMTP, FTP, and AMQP. The app is built to integrate with RabbitMQ allowing users with messaging queues to set up and make remote communication requests to their apps.

aboutPage.title: About SMSWithoutBorders
aboutPage.intro: SMSWithoutBorders (SWOB) is dedicated to researching, developing and promoting secure and accessible communication tools that function even without an internet connection.
history: The SMSWithoutBorders project began in 2021 and became a tool for fighting internet shutdowns in 2022, thanks to a grant from Internews and continued funding from the Open Technology Fund (OTF).

SMSWithoutBorders began with a single Android client called SWOB (short for SMSWithoutBorders), which was later renamed RelaySMS. In 2023, we began developing DekuSMS, an SMS messaging app with support for end-to-end encryption.

At that point, we had been using a Raspberry Pi and USB dongles to forward SMS messages for RelaySMS. This was inefficient due to power and other logistical issues. The service's downtime was extremely high, which led to low and continuously slow uptake.
We later moved the forwarding to DekuSMS, which performed better and reduced downtime by more than 90%. This improved the experience for first-time users and brought some uptake to the service.

Our experience in developing RelaySMS stems from having lived through internet shutdowns imposed for political reasons. One shutdown lasted more than 90 days in two regions of the country, setting an African record. This was in Cameroon in 2016.
useCases: RelaySMS is an open-source communication platform that aims to enable messaging across the internet using SMS messages. This is most useful in places without an active internet connection, which is common both in remote areas and during periods of unrest.

It is well established that governments weaponize the internet against their own people by shutting it down, completely or in some cases partially. This hinders people's ability to get news and life-saving information. It also hinders commerce and safe, secure communication. In these circumstances, tools like VPNs and other major circumvention techniques do not work, because they need some internet access to function.

It is for these circumstances that we are developing RelaySMS. While we know SMS messages are sometimes blocked during periods of unrest, SMS is usually restored faster than internet connections. This could be because adversaries may not yet consider SMS messaging a threat (beyond local person-to-person communication).
